title: Centor criteria
subtitle: Alternative acute sore-throat score
summary: Centor estimates likelihood of group A streptococcal infection and is not an airway or sepsis rule-out tool.

criteria.label: Tender anterior cervical lymphadenopathy
criteria.description: Painful/tender nodes at the front of the neck.

results.label: Antibiotics generally not indicated
actions: Supportive care: paracetamol or ibuprofen for analgesia and fever; adequate fluids; throat lozenges if tolerated
Arrange GP or telephone review within 48 hours if symptoms do not improve or worsen

results.label: More likely to benefit
interpretation: The patient is more likely to benefit from an immediate or back-up antibiotic, depending on clinical findings and local guidance.
actions: Prescribe antibiotic per local formulary guidance (e.g., penicillin V or amoxicillin-clavulanate); document choice and patient counseling
Alternatively, issue back-up antibiotic prescription with safety-netting for worsening or non-improvement within 48 hours
Assess separately for airway compromise, deep-neck infection (dysphagia, drooling, stridor), and hydration status; escalate if present

overrides: Assess airway, hydration and deep-neck infection separately.
Follow the Northern Ireland Primary Care Antimicrobial MicroGuide.
limitations: Do not use as a standalone prescribing instruction.
